"""
Production rate limiting for ClipCraft.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)


# --- Demo ---
print("=== Rate Limiting Demo for ClipCraft ===\
")

# Simulate requests from different users
users = [
    ("user_free_1", "free"),
    ("user_pro_1", "pro"),
    ("user_enterprise_1", "enterprise"),
]

for user_id, tier in users:
    print(f"User: {{user_id}} ({{tier}} tier)")

        status = "ALLOWED" if allowed else "BLOCKED"
        print(f"  Request {{i+1}}: {{status}} | {{info}}")
        if not allowed:

    print()

GenAI-2 BUILD: AI-SaaS-Produkt

Baue ein Video-Generierungs-SaaS

Baue ClipCraft — einen produktionsreifen Video-Generierungsdienst mit asynchronen Job-Queues, Fortschrittsverfolgung und einem FastAPI-Backend, das Text-zu-Video-Modelle orchestriert.
75 Min. Fortgeschritten / Praxisorientiert Du wirst ein echtes Produkt bauen und deployen

Was du bauen wirst

In dieser Lektion baust du ClipCraft — ein Video-Generierungs-SaaS. Nutzer senden Text-Prompts, dein Server leitet die Anfrage an ein Text-zu-Video-Modell weiter (Runway, Pika oder Stability AI Video), verwaltet den lang laufenden Generierungsprozess über eine asynchrone Job-Queue, streamt Fortschrittsupdates und liefert das fertige Video aus. Du implementierst den kompletten Stack: API-Server, Video-Verarbeitungspipeline, Job-Management, Fortschrittsverfolgung und Deployment.

Video-Generierung unterscheidet sich grundlegend von Bild-Generierung. Ein einzelnes Video kann 30 Sekunden bis 5 Minuten zur Erzeugung benötigen, was bedeutet, dass du kein einfaches Request-Response-Muster verwenden kannst. Stattdessen brauchst du eine asynchrone Architektur mit Job-Queues, Status-Polling und Webhook-Benachrichtigungen.

ClipCraft — Vollständiger Projektüberblick

Komponente Technologie

Video-GenerierungRunway Gen-3, Pika Labs oder Stability AI Video (über API)

DeploymentDocker + beliebiger Cloud-Anbieter

Teil 1: Wie Video-Generierungs-APIs funktionieren

Text-zu-Video-Modelle erweitern Diffusionstechniken von Bildern auf zeitliche Sequenzen. Statt einen einzelnen Frame zu entrauschen, entrauschen sie ein raumzeitliches Volumen — und erzeugen dabei mehrere kohärente Frames, die natürlich ineinander übergehen. Das ist um Größenordnungen aufwändiger als Bild-Generierung und dauert deutlich länger.

Vergleich der Video-Generierungs-APIs (2024–2025)

Anbieter Modell Kosten pro Video Dauer / Auflösung
RunwayGen-3 Alpha$0,25–$1,005–10s / bis zu 1280×768
Pika LabsPika 1.0$0,20–$0,803–4s / bis zu 1024×1024
Stability AIStable Video Diffusion$0,10–$0,504s / 576×1024
Luma AIDream Machine$0,30–$0,905s / bis zu 1360×752

Wesentlicher Unterschied zur Bild-Generierung

Bild-Generierung liefert ein Ergebnis in 2–10 Sekunden. Video-Generierung dauert 30 Sekunden bis 5 Minuten. Das bedeutet, du kannst keine HTTP-Verbindung offen halten und warten. Du brauchst:

  • Job-Queue: Die Anfrage annehmen, sofort eine Job-ID zurückgeben, im Hintergrund verarbeiten
  • Fortschrittsverfolgung: Clients den Status abfragen lassen oder Webhook-Callbacks empfangen lassen
  • Retry-Logik: Lang laufende Aufgaben schlagen häufiger fehl — du musst Wiederholungsversuche sauber handhaben
  • Ressourcenmanagement: Gleichzeitige Jobs begrenzen, um Kosten zu kontrollieren und Überlastung zu vermeiden

Das architektonische Muster lautet: annehmen → einreihen → verarbeiten → benachrichtigen. Lass uns jeden Baustein aufbauen.

Teil 2: Video-Verarbeitungspipeline

Bevor wir externe APIs einbinden, wollen wir verstehen, wie Video-Frames funktionieren. Ein Video ist eine Sequenz von Bild-Frames, die in schneller Abfolge abgespielt werden. Jeder Frame ist ein NumPy-Array aus Pixeldaten. Der folgende Code zeigt, wie man Video-Frames programmatisch erzeugt und verarbeitet.

Python 

# processing.py - Video frame generation and processing

import numpy as np
import time

class VideoFrameProcessor:
    """Generate and process video frames using NumPy."""

    @staticmethod
    def generate_gradient_frames(width, height, num_frames, fps=24):
        """Generate a sequence of gradient frames that animate over time."""
        frames = []
        for i in range(num_frames):
            frame = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
            t = i / num_frames  # normalized time 0..1

            for y in range(height):
                for x in range(width):
                    # Red channel: horizontal sweep that shifts over time
                    r = int(255 * ((x / width + t) % 1.0))
                    # Green channel: vertical pulse
                    g = int(255 * ((y / height + t * 0.5) % 1.0))
                    # Blue channel: radial wave from center
                    cx, cy = width / 2, height / 2
                    dist = ((x - cx)**2 + (y - cy)**2) ** 0.5
                    max_dist = (cx**2 + cy**2) ** 0.5
                    b = int(127 + 128 * np.sin(dist / max_dist * 6.28 - t * 6.28))
                    frame[y, x] = [r, g, b]

            frames.append(frame)
        return frames

    @staticmethod
    def apply_fade_transition(frames, fade_length=5):
        """Apply a fade-in at the start and fade-out at the end."""
        result = []
        total = len(frames)
        for i, frame in enumerate(frames):
            factor = 1.0
            if i < fade_length:
                factor = i / fade_length
            elif i >= total - fade_length:
                factor = (total - 1 - i) / fade_length
            faded = (frame.astype(np.float64) * factor).astype(np.uint8)
            result.append(faded)
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def compute_frame_stats(frames):
        """Compute statistics across all frames."""
        brightnesses = []
        for frame in frames:
            avg = frame.mean()
            brightnesses.append(round(float(avg), 2))

        return {
            "num_frames": len(frames),
            "resolution": f"{frames[0].shape[1]}x{frames[0].shape[0]}",
            "avg_brightness": round(np.mean(brightnesses), 2),
            "min_brightness": min(brightnesses),
            "max_brightness": max(brightnesses),
            "total_pixels": frames[0].shape[0] * frames[0].shape[1] * len(frames),
            "memory_mb": round(sum(f.nbytes for f in frames) / (1024*1024), 2)
        }

    @staticmethod
    def add_text_overlay_region(frame, x, y, box_w, box_h, color=(255, 255, 255)):
        """Add a colored rectangle region (simulating text overlay area)."""
        result = frame.copy()
        y_end = min(y + box_h, frame.shape[0])
        x_end = min(x + box_w, frame.shape[1])
        # Semi-transparent overlay
        overlay = result[y:y_end, x:x_end].astype(np.float64)
        overlay = overlay * 0.5 + np.array(color, dtype=np.float64) * 0.5
        result[y:y_end, x:x_end] = overlay.astype(np.uint8)
        return result

    ("720p", 1280, 720, 24, 5),

Teil 3: Asynchrone Job-Queue

Video-Generierung dauert zu lange für synchrones HTTP. Wir brauchen eine Job-Queue, die Anfragen annimmt, sie im Hintergrund verarbeitet und Clients den Status prüfen lässt. Das ist das zentrale architektonische Muster für jede lang laufende Aufgabe in einem SaaS-Produkt.

Python 

# job_queue.py - Async job queue for video generation

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class JobStatus:
    PENDING = "pending"
    PROCESSING = "processing"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

class VideoJob:
    """Represents a single video generation job."""

    def __init__(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        self.id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.style = style
        self.duration_sec = duration_sec
        self.resolution = resolution
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.status = JobStatus.PENDING
        self.progress = 0
        self.created_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.started_at = None
        self.completed_at = None
        self.result_url = None
        self.error = None
        self.retry_count = 0
        self.max_retries = 3

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "prompt": self.prompt[:40],
            "status": self.status,
            "progress": self.progress,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "started_at": self.started_at,
            "completed_at": self.completed_at,
            "result_url": self.result_url,
            "error": self.error
        }


class JobQueue:
    """In-process job queue for video generation tasks."""

    def __init__(self, max_concurrent=3):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.queue = []        # pending job IDs
        self.active = []       # currently processing job IDs
        self.max_concurrent = max_concurrent

    def submit(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        """Submit a new video generation job. Returns job ID."""
        job = VideoJob(prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id)
        self.jobs[job.id] = job
        self.queue.append(job.id)
        return job.id

    def get_status(self, job_id):
        """Get current status of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job.to_dict()

    def process_next(self):
        """Try to start the next pending job. Returns job or None."""
        if len(self.active) >= self.max_concurrent:
            return None
        if not self.queue:
            return None

        job_id = self.queue.pop(0)
        job = self.jobs[job_id]
        job.status = JobStatus.PROCESSING
        job.started_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.active.append(job_id)
        return job

    def update_progress(self, job_id, progress):
        """Update job progress (0-100)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.progress = min(progress, 100)

    def complete_job(self, job_id, result_url):
        """Mark job as completed with result URL."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.status = JobStatus.COMPLETED
            job.progress = 100
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            job.result_url = result_url
            if job_id in self.active:
                self.active.remove(job_id)

    def fail_job(self, job_id, error):
        """Mark job as failed. Re-queue if retries remain."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)

        job.retry_count += 1
        if job.retry_count < job.max_retries:
            job.status = JobStatus.PENDING
            job.progress = 0
            self.queue.append(job_id)
            return f"Retrying ({job.retry_count}/{job.max_retries})"
        else:
            job.status = JobStatus.FAILED
            job.error = error
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            return "Max retries exceeded"

    def cancel_job(self, job_id):
        """Cancel a pending or active job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return False
        job.status = JobStatus.CANCELLED
        job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        if job_id in self.queue:
            self.queue.remove(job_id)
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)
        return True

    def get_queue_stats(self):
        """Get overall queue statistics."""
        statuses = {}
        for job in self.jobs.values():
            statuses[job.status] = statuses.get(job.status, 0) + 1
        return {
            "total_jobs": len(self.jobs),
            "queue_length": len(self.queue),
            "active_jobs": len(self.active),
            "max_concurrent": self.max_concurrent,
            "by_status": statuses
        }


# --- Demo: Simulate a video generation workload ---
queue = JobQueue(max_concurrent=2)

print("=== ClipCraft Job Queue Demo ===\
")

# Submit several jobs
prompts = [
    ("A serene lake at sunset with mountains", "cinematic", 5),
    ("Robot dancing in a neon city", "anime", 4),
    ("Aerial flyover of a tropical island", "drone", 8),
    ("A flower blooming in timelapse", "macro", 3),
    ("Astronaut walking on Mars", "cinematic", 6),
]

print("Submitting 5 video generation jobs:")
job_ids = []
for prompt, style, dur in prompts:
    jid = queue.submit(prompt, style, dur, "1280x720", "user_demo")
    job_ids.append(jid)
    print(f"  Job {jid}: '{prompt[:35]}...' ({dur}s, {style})")

print(f"\
Queue stats: {queue.get_queue_stats()}")

# Process jobs step by step
print("\
--- Processing Loop ---\
")

step = 0
while queue.queue or queue.active:
    step += 1

    # Start next jobs if capacity available
    while len(queue.active) < queue.max_concurrent and queue.queue:
        job = queue.process_next()
        if job:
            print(f"Step {step}: STARTED job {job.id} "
                  f"({job.prompt[:25]}...)")

    # Simulate progress on active jobs
    for jid in list(queue.active):
        job = queue.jobs[jid]
        job.progress += 35  # simulate chunk of progress

        if job.progress >= 100:
            # Simulate: 1 in 5 chance of failure on first attempt
            if job.retry_count == 0 and job.id == job_ids[2]:
                msg = queue.fail_job(jid, "GPU timeout")
                print(f"Step {step}: FAILED job {jid} -> {msg}")
            else:
                url = f"https://cdn.clipcraft.dev/v/{jid}.mp4"
                queue.complete_job(jid, url)
                print(f"Step {step}: COMPLETED job {jid} "
                      f"-> {url}")
        else:
            queue.update_progress(jid, job.progress)
            print(f"Step {step}: job {jid} progress: "
                  f"{job.progress}%")

print(f"\
--- Final Results ---\
")
for jid in job_ids:
    status = queue.get_status(jid)
    print(f"Job {jid}: {status['status']}"
          f" | progress: {status['progress']}%"

Teil 4: Fortschrittsverfolgung

Clients müssen wissen, wie weit ihr Video fortgeschritten ist. Wir unterstützen zwei Muster: Polling (der Client prüft periodisch) und Webhooks (der Server sendet aktiv Updates). Beide sind für ein produktionsreifes SaaS unverzichtbar. Der folgende Code zeigt den Fortschritts-Tracker mit simulierter Webhook-Zustellung.

Python 

# progress.py - Progress tracking with polling and webhooks

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class ProgressTracker:
    """Track video generation progress with polling and webhook support."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.webhook_log = []  # simulated webhook deliveries

    def register_job(self, job_id, webhook_url=None):
        """Register a job for progress tracking."""
        self.jobs[job_id] = {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "progress": 0,
            "stage": "queued",
            "webhook_url": webhook_url,
            "events": [],
            "started": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }

    def update(self, job_id, progress, stage, message=""):
        """Update progress and optionally fire webhook."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return

        job["progress"] = progress
        job["stage"] = stage

        event = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "progress": progress,
            "stage": stage,
            "message": message
        }
        job["events"].append(event)

        # Fire webhook if configured
        if job["webhook_url"]:
            self._fire_webhook(job_id, event)

    def _fire_webhook(self, job_id, event):
        """Simulate sending a webhook notification."""
        payload = {
            "event": "video.progress",
            "job_id": job_id,
            "data": event,
            "delivery_id": str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        }
        self.webhook_log.append(payload)

    def poll(self, job_id):
        """Client polls for current status (the polling endpoint)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return {"error": "Job not found"}
        return {
            "job_id": job["job_id"],
            "progress": job["progress"],
            "stage": job["stage"],
            "latest_event": job["events"][-1] if job["events"] else None
        }

    def get_full_history(self, job_id):
        """Get the full event history of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job["events"]

Teil 5: Der FastAPI-Server

Das ist das Herzstück von ClipCraft — der API-Server, der Job-Queue, Fortschrittsverfolgung, Video-Verarbeitung und Abrechnung zusammenführt. Der wesentliche Unterschied zu einem Bild-Generierungsserver ist das asynchrone Muster: Der Endpoint /api/generate antwortet sofort mit einer Job-ID, und Clients fragen /api/jobs/{id} für den Fortschritt ab.

app/main.py
"""ClipCraft API Server - Video Generation SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header, BackgroundTasks
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Optional
import uuid
import asyncio
import time

from .config import settings
from .video_service import VideoService
from .job_queue import JobQueue, JobStatus
from .progress import ProgressTracker
from .billing import BillingSystem

app = FastAPI(title="ClipCraft API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

# Initialize services
video_service = VideoService(
    provider=settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
    api_key=settings.VIDEO_API_KEY
)
job_queue = JobQueue(max_concurrent=settings.MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS)
progress_tracker = ProgressTracker()
billing = BillingSystem()


# --- Request/Response Models ---
class GenerateRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str = Field(..., min_length=3, max_length=500)
    style: str = Field(default="cinematic")
    duration: int = Field(default=5, ge=2, le=15)
    resolution: str = Field(default="1280x720")
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None

class JobResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    message: str
    poll_url: str

class JobStatusResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    progress: int
    stage: str
    result_url: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    estimated_remaining_sec: Optional[int] = None


# --- API key authentication ---
async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    user = billing.get_user_by_key(x_api_key)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key")
    return user


# --- Background video generation task ---
async def process_video_job(job_id: str):
    """Background task that processes a video generation job."""
    job = job_queue.jobs.get(job_id)
    if not job:
        return

    try:
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 5, "initializing",
                                "Loading model and preparing generation")

        # Call the video generation API
        result = await video_service.generate(
            prompt=job.prompt,
            style=job.style,
            duration_sec=job.duration_sec,
            resolution=job.resolution,
            progress_callback=lambda p, s, m:
                progress_tracker.update(job_id, p, s, m)
        )

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 95, "uploading",
                                "Uploading to CDN")

        video_url = result["video_url"]
        job_queue.complete_job(job_id, video_url)

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 100, "completed",
                                "Video ready for download")

        billing.record_generation(
            job.user_id, job.prompt,
            result["cost"], job.resolution
        )

    except Exception as e:
        msg = job_queue.fail_job(job_id, str(e))
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 0, "failed", str(e))


# --- Endpoints ---
@app.post("/api/generate", response_model=JobResponse)
async def generate_video(req: GenerateRequest,
                         background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
                         user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Submit a video generation job. Returns immediately with a job ID."""
    # Check billing limits
    can, reason = billing.can_generate(user["id"])
    if not can:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail=reason)

    # Submit to job queue
    job_id = job_queue.submit(
        prompt=req.prompt,
        style=req.style,
        duration_sec=req.duration,
        resolution=req.resolution,
        user_id=user["id"]
    )

    # Register progress tracking
    progress_tracker.register_job(job_id, webhook_url=req.webhook_url)

    # Start processing in the background
    job = job_queue.process_next()
    if job:
        background_tasks.add_task(process_video_job, job.id)

    return JobResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status="pending",
        message="Video generation job submitted",
        poll_url=f"/api/jobs/{job_id}"
    )


@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}", response_model=JobStatusResponse)
async def get_job_status(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Poll for job status and progress."""
    status = job_queue.get_status(job_id)
    if not status:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")

    poll_data = progress_tracker.poll(job_id)
    estimated = None
    if poll_data and poll_data.get("progress", 0) > 0:
        pct = poll_data["progress"]
        if pct < 100:
            estimated = int((100 - pct) * 1.5)

    return JobStatusResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status=status["status"],
        progress=status.get("progress", 0),
        stage=poll_data.get("stage", "unknown") if poll_data else "unknown",
        result_url=status.get("result_url"),
        error=status.get("error"),
        estimated_remaining_sec=estimated
    )


@app.delete("/api/jobs/{job_id}")
async def cancel_job(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Cancel a pending or active job."""
    success = job_queue.cancel_job(job_id)
    if not success:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")
    return {"message": "Job cancelled", "job_id": job_id}


@app.get("/api/jobs")
async def list_jobs(user=Depends(get_user)):
    """List all jobs for the authenticated user."""
    user_jobs = [
        job.to_dict() for job in job_queue.jobs.values()
        if job.user_id == user["id"]
    ]
    return {"jobs": user_jobs, "total": len(user_jobs)}


@app.get("/api/queue/stats")
async def queue_stats():
    """Get queue statistics (admin endpoint)."""
    return job_queue.get_queue_stats()


@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {
        "status": "ok",
        "provider": settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
        "queue": job_queue.get_queue_stats()
    }

Teil 11: Verbindung zu einem eigenen LLM

Bisher haben wir Drittanbieter-APIs verwendet. Aber die eigentliche Stärke — und die eigentlichen Margen — entstehen, wenn du eigene Modelle betreibst. Das eliminiert die API-Kosten pro Anfrage, gibt dir volle Kontrolle über Latenz und Datenschutz und erlaubt es dir, Modelle für deinen konkreten Anwendungsfall feinabzustimmen.

Drei wesentliche Ansätze für Self-Hosting:

  • vLLM — höchster Durchsatz, OpenAI-kompatible API, am besten für Produktion
  • Ollama — einfachste Einrichtung, ideal für Entwicklung und kleine Deployments
  • llama.cpp — am leichtgewichtigsten, läuft auf der CPU, ideal für Edge-Deployment

Für Video-Generierung kannst du Modelle wie CogVideoX, Mochi oder AnimateDiff selbst hosten:

Teil 13: Rate Limiting & API-Schutz

Jedes produktionsreife SaaS braucht Rate Limiting, um Missbrauch zu verhindern, Kosten zu kontrollieren und faire Nutzung sicherzustellen. Hier ist eine produktionsreife Implementierung:

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ClipCraft
"""
Production rate limiting for ClipCraft.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)

Wichtigste Erkenntnisse

  • Async ist bei Video Pflicht: Video-Generierung dauert 30 Sekunden bis 5 Minuten. Du musst eine Job-Queue mit Hintergrundverarbeitung verwenden — synchrones HTTP läuft in ein Timeout.
  • Fortschrittsverfolgung schafft Vertrauen: Nutzer müssen sehen, dass etwas passiert. Biete sowohl Polling-Endpoints als auch Webhook-Callbacks für Flexibilität an.
  • Retry-Logik ist entscheidend: Lang laufende GPU-Aufgaben schlagen häufiger fehl als schnelle API-Aufrufe. Automatische Wiederholungsversuche mit exponentiellem Backoff halten deinen Dienst zuverlässig.
  • Nebenläufigkeit kontrollieren, um Kosten zu kontrollieren: Begrenze die Anzahl gleichzeitiger Jobs. Jedes Video kostet $0,10–$1,00 an API-Gebühren — unkontrollierte Nebenläufigkeit kann dein Budget in Minuten aufbrauchen.
  • Video ist 10–50x teurer als Bilder: Preise deine Tarifstufen entsprechend. Ein 10 $/Monat-Plan, der 100 Bilder erlaubt, erlaubt vielleicht nur 10–20 Videos.
  • FFmpeg ist dein bester Freund: Nutze es für Transcodierung, Auflösungsänderungen, Wasserzeichen und Formatkonvertierung. Es läuft überall und beherrscht jeden Codec.

Les modèles text-to-video étendent les techniques de diffusion des images aux séquences temporelles. Au lieu de débruiter une seule image, ils débruitent un volume spatio-temporel — produisant plusieurs images cohérentes qui s'enchaînent naturellement. # processing.py - Video frame generation and processing

import numpy as np
import time

class VideoFrameProcessor:
    """Generate and process video frames using NumPy."""

    @staticmethod
    def generate_gradient_frames(width, height, num_frames, fps=24):
        """Generate a sequence of gradient frames that animate over time."""
        frames = []
        for i in range(num_frames):
            frame = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
            t = i / num_frames  # normalized time 0..1

            for y in range(height):
                for x in range(width):
                    # Red channel: horizontal sweep that shifts over time
                    r = int(255 * ((x / width + t) % 1.0))
                    # Green channel: vertical pulse
                    g = int(255 * ((y / height + t * 0.5) % 1.0))
                    # Blue channel: radial wave from center
                    cx, cy = width / 2, height / 2
                    dist = ((x - cx)**2 + (y - cy)**2) ** 0.5
                    max_dist = (cx**2 + cy**2) ** 0.5
                    b = int(127 + 128 * np.sin(dist / max_dist * 6.28 - t * 6.28))
                    frame[y, x] = [r, g, b]

            frames.append(frame)
        return frames

    @staticmethod
    def apply_fade_transition(frames, fade_length=5):
        """Apply a fade-in at the start and fade-out at the end."""
        result = []
        total = len(frames)
        for i, frame in enumerate(frames):
            factor = 1.0
            if i < fade_length:
                factor = i / fade_length
            elif i >= total - fade_length:
                factor = (total - 1 - i) / fade_length
            faded = (frame.astype(np.float64) * factor).astype(np.uint8)
            result.append(faded)
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def compute_frame_stats(frames):
        """Compute statistics across all frames."""
        brightnesses = []
        for frame in frames:
            avg = frame.mean()
            brightnesses.append(round(float(avg), 2))

        return {
            "num_frames": len(frames),
            "resolution": f"{frames[0].shape[1]}x{frames[0].shape[0]}",
            "avg_brightness": round(np.mean(brightnesses), 2),
            "min_brightness": min(brightnesses),
            "max_brightness": max(brightnesses),
            "total_pixels": frames[0].shape[0] * frames[0].shape[1] * len(frames),
            "memory_mb": round(sum(f.nbytes for f in frames) / (1024*1024), 2)
        }

    @staticmethod
    def add_text_overlay_region(frame, x, y, box_w, box_h, color=(255, 255, 255)):
        """Add a colored rectangle region (simulating text overlay area)."""
        result = frame.copy()
        y_end = min(y + box_h, frame.shape[0])
        x_end = min(x + box_w, frame.shape[1])
        # Semi-transparent overlay
        overlay = result[y:y_end, x:x_end].astype(np.float64)
        overlay = overlay * 0.5 + np.array(color, dtype=np.float64) * 0.5
        result[y:y_end, x:x_end] = overlay.astype(np.uint8)
        return result

# job_queue.py - Async job queue for video generation

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class JobStatus:
    PENDING = "pending"
    PROCESSING = "processing"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

class VideoJob:
    """Represents a single video generation job."""

    def __init__(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        self.id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.style = style
        self.duration_sec = duration_sec
        self.resolution = resolution
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.status = JobStatus.PENDING
        self.progress = 0
        self.created_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.started_at = None
        self.completed_at = None
        self.result_url = None
        self.error = None
        self.retry_count = 0
        self.max_retries = 3

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "prompt": self.prompt[:40],
            "status": self.status,
            "progress": self.progress,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "started_at": self.started_at,
            "completed_at": self.completed_at,
            "result_url": self.result_url,
            "error": self.error
        }


class JobQueue:
    """In-process job queue for video generation tasks."""

    def __init__(self, max_concurrent=3):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.queue = []        # pending job IDs
        self.active = []       # currently processing job IDs
        self.max_concurrent = max_concurrent

    def submit(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        """Submit a new video generation job. Returns job ID."""
        job = VideoJob(prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id)
        self.jobs[job.id] = job
        self.queue.append(job.id)
        return job.id

    def get_status(self, job_id):
        """Get current status of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job.to_dict()

    def process_next(self):
        """Try to start the next pending job. Returns job or None."""
        if len(self.active) >= self.max_concurrent:
            return None
        if not self.queue:
            return None

        job_id = self.queue.pop(0)
        job = self.jobs[job_id]
        job.status = JobStatus.PROCESSING
        job.started_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.active.append(job_id)
        return job

    def update_progress(self, job_id, progress):
        """Update job progress (0-100)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.progress = min(progress, 100)

    def complete_job(self, job_id, result_url):
        """Mark job as completed with result URL."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.status = JobStatus.COMPLETED
            job.progress = 100
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            job.result_url = result_url
            if job_id in self.active:
                self.active.remove(job_id)

    def fail_job(self, job_id, error):
        """Mark job as failed. Re-queue if retries remain."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)

        job.retry_count += 1
        if job.retry_count < job.max_retries:
            job.status = JobStatus.PENDING
            job.progress = 0
            self.queue.append(job_id)
            return f"Retrying ({job.retry_count}/{job.max_retries})"
        else:
            job.status = JobStatus.FAILED
            job.error = error
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            return "Max retries exceeded"

    def cancel_job(self, job_id):
        """Cancel a pending or active job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return False
        job.status = JobStatus.CANCELLED
        job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        if job_id in self.queue:
            self.queue.remove(job_id)
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)
        return True

    def get_queue_stats(self):
        """Get overall queue statistics."""
        statuses = {}
        for job in self.jobs.values():
            statuses[job.status] = statuses.get(job.status, 0) + 1
        return {
            "total_jobs": len(self.jobs),
            "queue_length": len(self.queue),
            "active_jobs": len(self.active),
            "max_concurrent": self.max_concurrent,
            "by_status": statuses
        }

Partie 4 : Suivi de la Progression

Les clients doivent savoir où en est leur vidéo. Nous prenons en charge deux modèles : le polling (le client vérifie périodiquement) et les webhooks (le serveur pousse les mises à jour). Les deux sont essentiels pour un SaaS de production. Le code ci-dessous montre le tracker de progression avec une livraison de webhook simulée.

Python 

# progress.py - Progress tracking with polling and webhooks

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class ProgressTracker:
    """Track video generation progress with polling and webhook support."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.webhook_log = []  # simulated webhook deliveries

    def register_job(self, job_id, webhook_url=None):
        """Register a job for progress tracking."""
        self.jobs[job_id] = {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "progress": 0,
            "stage": "queued",
            "webhook_url": webhook_url,
            "events": [],
            "started": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }

    def update(self, job_id, progress, stage, message=""):
        """Update progress and optionally fire webhook."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return

        job["progress"] = progress
        job["stage"] = stage

        event = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "progress": progress,
            "stage": stage,
            "message": message
        }
        job["events"].append(event)

        # Fire webhook if configured
        if job["webhook_url"]:
            self._fire_webhook(job_id, event)

    def _fire_webhook(self, job_id, event):
        """Simulate sending a webhook notification."""
        payload = {
            "event": "video.progress",
            "job_id": job_id,
            "data": event,
            "delivery_id": str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        }
        self.webhook_log.append(payload)

    def poll(self, job_id):
        """Client polls for current status (the polling endpoint)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return {"error": "Job not found"}
        return {
            "job_id": job["job_id"],
            "progress": job["progress"],
            "stage": job["stage"],
            "latest_event": job["events"][-1] if job["events"] else None
        }

    def get_full_history(self, job_id):
        """Get the full event history of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job["events"]

    style: str = Field(default="cinematic")
    duration: int = Field(default=5, ge=2, le=15)
    resolution: str = Field(default="1280x720")
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None

class JobResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    message: str
    poll_url: str

class JobStatusResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    progress: int
    stage: str
    result_url: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    estimated_remaining_sec: Optional[int] = None


# --- API key authentication ---
async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    user = billing.get_user_by_key(x_api_key)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key")
    return user


# --- Background video generation task ---
async def process_video_job(job_id: str):
    """Background task that processes a video generation job."""
    job = job_queue.jobs.get(job_id)
    if not job:
        return

    try:
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 5, "initializing",
                                "Loading model and preparing generation")

        # Call the video generation API
        result = await video_service.generate(
            prompt=job.prompt,
            style=job.style,
            duration_sec=job.duration_sec,
            resolution=job.resolution,
            progress_callback=lambda p, s, m:
                progress_tracker.update(job_id, p, s, m)
        )

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 95, "uploading",
                                "Uploading to CDN")

        video_url = result["video_url"]
        job_queue.complete_job(job_id, video_url)

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 100, "completed",
                                "Video ready for download")

        billing.record_generation(
            job.user_id, job.prompt,
            result["cost"], job.resolution
        )

    except Exception as e:
        msg = job_queue.fail_job(job_id, str(e))
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 0, "failed", str(e))


# --- Endpoints ---
@app.post("/api/generate", response_model=JobResponse)
async def generate_video(req: GenerateRequest,
                         background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
                         user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Submit a video generation job. Returns immediately with a job ID."""
    # Check billing limits
    can, reason = billing.can_generate(user["id"])
    if not can:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail=reason)

    # Submit to job queue
    job_id = job_queue.submit(
        prompt=req.prompt,
        style=req.style,
        duration_sec=req.duration,
        resolution=req.resolution,
        user_id=user["id"]
    )

    # Register progress tracking
    progress_tracker.register_job(job_id, webhook_url=req.webhook_url)

    # Start processing in the background
    job = job_queue.process_next()
    if job:
        background_tasks.add_task(process_video_job, job.id)

    return JobResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status="pending",
        message="Video generation job submitted",
        poll_url=f"/api/jobs/{job_id}"
    )


@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}", response_model=JobStatusResponse)
async def get_job_status(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Poll for job status and progress."""
    status = job_queue.get_status(job_id)
    if not status:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")

    poll_data = progress_tracker.poll(job_id)
    estimated = None
    if poll_data and poll_data.get("progress", 0) > 0:
        pct = poll_data["progress"]
        if pct < 100:
            estimated = int((100 - pct) * 1.5)

    return JobStatusResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status=status["status"],
        progress=status.get("progress", 0),
        stage=poll_data.get("stage", "unknown") if poll_data else "unknown",
        result_url=status.get("result_url"),
        error=status.get("error"),
        estimated_remaining_sec=estimated
    )


@app.delete("/api/jobs/{job_id}")
async def cancel_job(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Cancel a pending or active job."""
    success = job_queue.cancel_job(job_id)
    if not success:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")
    return {"message": "Job cancelled", "job_id": job_id}


@app.get("/api/jobs")
async def list_jobs(user=Depends(get_user)):
    """List all jobs for the authenticated user."""
    user_jobs = [
        job.to_dict() for job in job_queue.jobs.values()
        if job.user_id == user["id"]
    ]
    return {"jobs": user_jobs, "total": len(user_jobs)}


@app.get("/api/queue/stats")
async def queue_stats():
    """Get queue statistics (admin endpoint)."""
    return job_queue.get_queue_stats()


@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {
        "status": "ok",
        "provider": settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
        "queue": job_queue.get_queue_stats()
    }

Partie 11 : Connectez-vous à Votre Propre LLM

Jusqu'ici, nous avons utilisé des API tierces. Mais la véritable puissance — et les véritables marges — apparaissent lorsque vous exécutez vos propres modèles. Cela élimine les coûts d'API par requête, vous donne un contrôle total sur la latence et la confidentialité, et vous permet d'affiner (fine-tune) des modèles pour votre cas d'usage spécifique.

Trois approches principales pour l'auto-hébergement :

  • vLLM — débit le plus élevé, API compatible OpenAI, idéal pour la production
  • Ollama — installation la plus simple, parfait pour le développement et un déploiement à petite échelle
  • llama.cpp — le plus léger, fonctionne sur CPU, idéal pour le déploiement en périphérie (edge)

Partie 13 : Limitation de Débit & Protection de l'API

Tout SaaS de production a besoin d'une limitation de débit pour prévenir les abus, contrôler les coûts et garantir un usage équitable. Voici une implémentation de niveau production :

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ClipCraft
"""
Production rate limiting for ClipCraft.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)

Points Clés à Retenir

  • L'asynchrone est obligatoire pour la vidéo : La génération vidéo prend 30 secondes à 5 minutes. Vous devez utiliser une file d'attente de tâches avec traitement en arrière-plan — le HTTP synchrone expirera.
  • Le suivi de la progression construit la confiance : Les utilisateurs doivent voir que quelque chose se passe. Proposez à la fois des endpoints de polling et des callbacks webhook pour plus de flexibilité.
  • La logique de nouvelle tentative est critique : Les tâches GPU de longue durée échouent plus souvent que les appels API rapides. Des nouvelles tentatives automatiques avec backoff exponentiel maintiennent la fiabilité de votre service.
  • Contrôlez la concurrence pour contrôler les coûts : Limitez le nombre de tâches simultanées. Chaque vidéo coûte $0.10–$1.00 en frais d'API — une concurrence incontrôlée peut épuiser votre budget en quelques minutes.
  • La vidéo coûte 10–50x plus cher que les images : Tarifez vos niveaux en conséquence. Un plan à 10$/mois qui permet 100 images pourrait ne permettre que 10–20 vidéos.
  • FFmpeg est votre meilleur ami : Utilisez-le pour le transcodage, les changements de résolution, le filigranage et la conversion de format. Il fonctionne partout et gère tous les codecs.

GenAI-2 BUILD: Prodotto AI SaaS

Costruisci un SaaS di Generazione Video

Costruisci ClipCraft — un servizio di generazione video pronto per la produzione con code di job asincrone, monitoraggio del progresso e un backend FastAPI che orchestra modelli text-to-video.
75 min Avanzato / Pratico Costruirai e distribuirai un prodotto reale

Cosa Costruirai

In questa lezione costruisci ClipCraft — un SaaS di generazione video. Gli utenti inviano prompt testuali, il tuo server smista la richiesta verso un modello text-to-video (Runway, Pika o Stability AI Video), gestisce il processo di generazione di lunga durata tramite una coda di job asincrona, trasmette aggiornamenti sul progresso e consegna il video finale. Implementerai l’intero stack: server API, pipeline di elaborazione video, gestione dei job, monitoraggio del progresso e deployment.

La generazione video è fondamentalmente diversa dalla generazione di immagini. Un singolo video può richiedere da 30 secondi a 5 minuti per essere prodotto, il che significa che non puoi usare un semplice modello richiesta-risposta. Hai invece bisogno di un’architettura asincrona con code di job, polling dello stato e notifiche webhook.

ClipCraft — Panoramica Completa del Progetto

Coda di JobCoda asincrona in-process (dev) / Redis + Celery (prod)

Elaborazione VideoNumPy (calcoli sui frame) + FFmpeg (codifica)
DatabaseSQLite (dev) / PostgreSQL (prod)
FrontendHTML + vanilla JS

Struttura del Progetto

Crea questa struttura di cartelle sulla tua macchina. Ogni file è spiegato in questa lezione.

Parte 1: Come Funzionano le API di Generazione Video

I modelli text-to-video estendono le tecniche di diffusione dalle immagini alle sequenze temporali. Invece di rimuovere il rumore da un singolo frame, rimuovono il rumore da un volume spazio-temporale — producendo più frame coerenti che scorrono in modo naturale. Questo è di ordini di grandezza più costoso della generazione di immagini e richiede molto più tempo.

Confronto tra le API di Generazione Video (2024–2025)

Provider Modello Costo per video Durata / Risoluzione
RunwayGen-3 Alpha$0.25–$1.005–10s / fino a 1280×768
Pika LabsPika 1.0$0.20–$0.803–4s / fino a 1024×1024
Stability AIStable Video Diffusion$0.10–$0.504s / 576×1024
Luma AIDream Machine$0.30–$0.905s / fino a 1360×752

Differenza Chiave rispetto alla Generazione di Immagini

La generazione di immagini restituisce un risultato in 2–10 secondi. La generazione video richiede da 30 secondi a 5 minuti. Questo significa che non puoi mantenere aperta una connessione HTTP e aspettare. Hai bisogno di:

  • Coda di Job: Accetta la richiesta, restituisci immediatamente un ID job, elabora in background
  • Monitoraggio del Progresso: Permetti ai client di interrogare lo stato o ricevere callback webhook
  • Logica di Retry: I task di lunga durata falliscono più spesso — devi gestire i tentativi di ripetizione con eleganza
  • Gestione delle Risorse: Limita i job concorrenti per controllare i costi e prevenire il sovraccarico

Il pattern architetturale è: accetta → accoda → elabora → notifica. Costruiamo ogni componente.

Parte 2: Pipeline di Elaborazione Video

Prima di integrare API esterne, cerchiamo di capire come funzionano i frame video. Un video è una sequenza di frame immagine riprodotti in rapida successione. Ogni frame è un array NumPy di dati pixel. Il codice qui sotto dimostra come generare ed elaborare frame video in modo programmatico.

Python 

# processing.py - Video frame generation and processing

import numpy as np
import time

class VideoFrameProcessor:
    """Generate and process video frames using NumPy."""

    @staticmethod
    def generate_gradient_frames(width, height, num_frames, fps=24):
        """Generate a sequence of gradient frames that animate over time."""
        frames = []
        for i in range(num_frames):
            frame = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
            t = i / num_frames  # normalized time 0..1

            for y in range(height):
                for x in range(width):
                    # Red channel: horizontal sweep that shifts over time
                    r = int(255 * ((x / width + t) % 1.0))
                    # Green channel: vertical pulse
                    g = int(255 * ((y / height + t * 0.5) % 1.0))
                    # Blue channel: radial wave from center
                    cx, cy = width / 2, height / 2
                    dist = ((x - cx)**2 + (y - cy)**2) ** 0.5
                    max_dist = (cx**2 + cy**2) ** 0.5
                    b = int(127 + 128 * np.sin(dist / max_dist * 6.28 - t * 6.28))
                    frame[y, x] = [r, g, b]

            frames.append(frame)
        return frames

    @staticmethod
    def apply_fade_transition(frames, fade_length=5):
        """Apply a fade-in at the start and fade-out at the end."""
        result = []
        total = len(frames)
        for i, frame in enumerate(frames):
            factor = 1.0
            if i < fade_length:
                factor = i / fade_length
            elif i >= total - fade_length:
                factor = (total - 1 - i) / fade_length
            faded = (frame.astype(np.float64) * factor).astype(np.uint8)
            result.append(faded)
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def compute_frame_stats(frames):
        """Compute statistics across all frames."""
        brightnesses = []
        for frame in frames:
            avg = frame.mean()
            brightnesses.append(round(float(avg), 2))

        return {
            "num_frames": len(frames),
            "resolution": f"{frames[0].shape[1]}x{frames[0].shape[0]}",
            "avg_brightness": round(np.mean(brightnesses), 2),
            "min_brightness": min(brightnesses),
            "max_brightness": max(brightnesses),
            "total_pixels": frames[0].shape[0] * frames[0].shape[1] * len(frames),
            "memory_mb": round(sum(f.nbytes for f in frames) / (1024*1024), 2)
        }

    @staticmethod
    def add_text_overlay_region(frame, x, y, box_w, box_h, color=(255, 255, 255)):
        """Add a colored rectangle region (simulating text overlay area)."""
        result = frame.copy()
        y_end = min(y + box_h, frame.shape[0])
        x_end = min(x + box_w, frame.shape[1])
        # Semi-transparent overlay
        overlay = result[y:y_end, x:x_end].astype(np.float64)
        overlay = overlay * 0.5 + np.array(color, dtype=np.float64) * 0.5
        result[y:y_end, x:x_end] = overlay.astype(np.uint8)
        return result

Parte 3: Coda di Job Asincrona

La generazione video richiede troppo tempo per l’HTTP sincrono. Abbiamo bisogno di una coda di job che accetti le richieste, le elabori in background e permetta ai client di verificare lo stato. Questo è il pattern architetturale fondamentale per qualsiasi task di lunga durata in un prodotto SaaS.

Python 

# job_queue.py - Async job queue for video generation

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class JobStatus:
    PENDING = "pending"
    PROCESSING = "processing"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

class VideoJob:
    """Represents a single video generation job."""

    def __init__(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        self.id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.style = style
        self.duration_sec = duration_sec
        self.resolution = resolution
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.status = JobStatus.PENDING
        self.progress = 0
        self.created_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.started_at = None
        self.completed_at = None
        self.result_url = None
        self.error = None
        self.retry_count = 0
        self.max_retries = 3

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "prompt": self.prompt[:40],
            "status": self.status,
            "progress": self.progress,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "started_at": self.started_at,
            "completed_at": self.completed_at,
            "result_url": self.result_url,
            "error": self.error
        }


class JobQueue:
    """In-process job queue for video generation tasks."""

    def __init__(self, max_concurrent=3):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.queue = []        # pending job IDs
        self.active = []       # currently processing job IDs
        self.max_concurrent = max_concurrent

    def submit(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        """Submit a new video generation job. Returns job ID."""
        job = VideoJob(prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id)
        self.jobs[job.id] = job
        self.queue.append(job.id)
        return job.id

    def get_status(self, job_id):
        """Get current status of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job.to_dict()

    def process_next(self):
        """Try to start the next pending job. Returns job or None."""
        if len(self.active) >= self.max_concurrent:
            return None
        if not self.queue:
            return None

        job_id = self.queue.pop(0)
        job = self.jobs[job_id]
        job.status = JobStatus.PROCESSING
        job.started_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.active.append(job_id)
        return job

    def update_progress(self, job_id, progress):
        """Update job progress (0-100)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.progress = min(progress, 100)

    def complete_job(self, job_id, result_url):
        """Mark job as completed with result URL."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.status = JobStatus.COMPLETED
            job.progress = 100
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            job.result_url = result_url
            if job_id in self.active:
                self.active.remove(job_id)

    def fail_job(self, job_id, error):
        """Mark job as failed. Re-queue if retries remain."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)

        job.retry_count += 1
        if job.retry_count < job.max_retries:
            job.status = JobStatus.PENDING
            job.progress = 0
            self.queue.append(job_id)
            return f"Retrying ({job.retry_count}/{job.max_retries})"
        else:
            job.status = JobStatus.FAILED
            job.error = error
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            return "Max retries exceeded"

    def cancel_job(self, job_id):
        """Cancel a pending or active job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return False
        job.status = JobStatus.CANCELLED
        job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        if job_id in self.queue:
            self.queue.remove(job_id)
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)
        return True

    def get_queue_stats(self):
        """Get overall queue statistics."""
        statuses = {}
        for job in self.jobs.values():
            statuses[job.status] = statuses.get(job.status, 0) + 1
        return {
            "total_jobs": len(self.jobs),
            "queue_length": len(self.queue),
            "active_jobs": len(self.active),
            "max_concurrent": self.max_concurrent,
            "by_status": statuses
        }


# --- Demo: Simulate a video generation workload ---

print("=== ClipCraft Job Queue Demo ===\
")

# Submit several jobs
prompts = [
    ("A serene lake at sunset with mountains", "cinematic", 5),
    ("Robot dancing in a neon city", "anime", 4),

Queue stats: {queue.get_queue_stats()}")

--- Processing Loop ---\
")

step = 0
while queue.queue or queue.active:
    step += 1

    # Start next jobs if capacity available
    while len(queue.active) < queue.max_concurrent and queue.queue:
        job = queue.process_next()
        if job:
            print(f"Step {step}: STARTED job {job.id} "
                  f"({job.prompt[:25]}...)")

    # Simulate progress on active jobs
    for jid in list(queue.active):
        job = queue.jobs[jid]

        if job.progress >= 100:

Parte 4: Monitoraggio del Progresso

I client devono sapere come sta procedendo il loro video. Supportiamo due pattern: polling (il client verifica periodicamente) e webhook (il server invia aggiornamenti). Entrambi sono essenziali per un SaaS di produzione. Il codice qui sotto dimostra il tracker di progresso con consegna simulata di webhook.

Python 

# progress.py - Progress tracking with polling and webhooks

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class ProgressTracker:
    """Track video generation progress with polling and webhook support."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.webhook_log = []  # simulated webhook deliveries

    def register_job(self, job_id, webhook_url=None):
        """Register a job for progress tracking."""
        self.jobs[job_id] = {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "progress": 0,
            "stage": "queued",
            "webhook_url": webhook_url,
            "events": [],
            "started": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }

    def update(self, job_id, progress, stage, message=""):
        """Update progress and optionally fire webhook."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return

        job["progress"] = progress
        job["stage"] = stage

        event = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "progress": progress,
            "stage": stage,
            "message": message
        }
        job["events"].append(event)

        # Fire webhook if configured
        if job["webhook_url"]:
            self._fire_webhook(job_id, event)

    def _fire_webhook(self, job_id, event):
        """Simulate sending a webhook notification."""
        payload = {
            "event": "video.progress",
            "job_id": job_id,
            "data": event,
            "delivery_id": str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        }
        self.webhook_log.append(payload)

    def poll(self, job_id):
        """Client polls for current status (the polling endpoint)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return {"error": "Job not found"}
        return {
            "job_id": job["job_id"],
            "progress": job["progress"],
            "stage": job["stage"],
            "latest_event": job["events"][-1] if job["events"] else None
        }

    def get_full_history(self, job_id):
        """Get the full event history of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job["events"]

Parte 5: Il Server FastAPI

Questo è il cuore di ClipCraft — il server API che collega la coda di job, il monitoraggio del progresso, l’elaborazione video e la fatturazione. La differenza chiave rispetto a un server di generazione immagini è il pattern asincrono: l’endpoint /api/generate restituisce immediatamente un ID job, e i client interrogano /api/jobs/{id} per il progresso.

app/main.py
"""ClipCraft API Server - Video Generation SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header, BackgroundTasks
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Optional
import uuid
import asyncio
import time

from .config import settings
from .video_service import VideoService
from .job_queue import JobQueue, JobStatus
from .progress import ProgressTracker
from .billing import BillingSystem

app = FastAPI(title="ClipCraft API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

# Initialize services
video_service = VideoService(
    provider=settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
    api_key=settings.VIDEO_API_KEY
)
job_queue = JobQueue(max_concurrent=settings.MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS)
progress_tracker = ProgressTracker()
billing = BillingSystem()


# --- Request/Response Models ---
class GenerateRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str = Field(..., min_length=3, max_length=500)
    style: str = Field(default="cinematic")
    duration: int = Field(default=5, ge=2, le=15)
    resolution: str = Field(default="1280x720")
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None

class JobResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    message: str
    poll_url: str

class JobStatusResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    progress: int
    stage: str
    result_url: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    estimated_remaining_sec: Optional[int] = None


# --- API key authentication ---
async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    user = billing.get_user_by_key(x_api_key)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key")
    return user


# --- Background video generation task ---
async def process_video_job(job_id: str):
    """Background task that processes a video generation job."""
    job = job_queue.jobs.get(job_id)
    if not job:
        return

    try:
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 5, "initializing",
                                "Loading model and preparing generation")

        # Call the video generation API
        result = await video_service.generate(
            prompt=job.prompt,
            style=job.style,
            duration_sec=job.duration_sec,
            resolution=job.resolution,
            progress_callback=lambda p, s, m:
                progress_tracker.update(job_id, p, s, m)
        )

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 95, "uploading",
                                "Uploading to CDN")

        video_url = result["video_url"]
        job_queue.complete_job(job_id, video_url)

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 100, "completed",
                                "Video ready for download")

        billing.record_generation(
            job.user_id, job.prompt,
            result["cost"], job.resolution
        )

    except Exception as e:
        msg = job_queue.fail_job(job_id, str(e))
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 0, "failed", str(e))


# --- Endpoints ---
@app.post("/api/generate", response_model=JobResponse)
async def generate_video(req: GenerateRequest,
                         background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
                         user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Submit a video generation job. Returns immediately with a job ID."""
    # Check billing limits
    can, reason = billing.can_generate(user["id"])
    if not can:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail=reason)

    # Submit to job queue
    job_id = job_queue.submit(
        prompt=req.prompt,
        style=req.style,
        duration_sec=req.duration,
        resolution=req.resolution,
        user_id=user["id"]
    )

    # Register progress tracking
    progress_tracker.register_job(job_id, webhook_url=req.webhook_url)

    # Start processing in the background
    job = job_queue.process_next()
    if job:
        background_tasks.add_task(process_video_job, job.id)

    return JobResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status="pending",
        message="Video generation job submitted",
        poll_url=f"/api/jobs/{job_id}"
    )


@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}", response_model=JobStatusResponse)
async def get_job_status(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Poll for job status and progress."""
    status = job_queue.get_status(job_id)
    if not status:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")

    poll_data = progress_tracker.poll(job_id)
    estimated = None
    if poll_data and poll_data.get("progress", 0) > 0:
        pct = poll_data["progress"]
        if pct < 100:
            estimated = int((100 - pct) * 1.5)

    return JobStatusResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status=status["status"],
        progress=status.get("progress", 0),
        stage=poll_data.get("stage", "unknown") if poll_data else "unknown",
        result_url=status.get("result_url"),
        error=status.get("error"),
        estimated_remaining_sec=estimated
    )


@app.delete("/api/jobs/{job_id}")
async def cancel_job(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Cancel a pending or active job."""
    success = job_queue.cancel_job(job_id)
    if not success:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")
    return {"message": "Job cancelled", "job_id": job_id}


@app.get("/api/jobs")
async def list_jobs(user=Depends(get_user)):
    """List all jobs for the authenticated user."""
    user_jobs = [
        job.to_dict() for job in job_queue.jobs.values()
        if job.user_id == user["id"]
    ]
    return {"jobs": user_jobs, "total": len(user_jobs)}


@app.get("/api/queue/stats")
async def queue_stats():
    """Get queue statistics (admin endpoint)."""
    return job_queue.get_queue_stats()


@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {
        "status": "ok",
        "provider": settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
        "queue": job_queue.get_queue_stats()
    }
