Parte 11: Collega il Tuo LLM

Finora abbiamo usato API di terze parti. Ma il vero potere — e i veri margini — arrivano quando esegui i tuoi modelli. Questo elimina i costi API per richiesta, ti dà pieno controllo su latenza e privacy, e ti permette di fare fine-tuning dei modelli per il tuo caso d’uso specifico.

Tre approcci principali per il self-hosting:

  • vLLM — throughput più elevato, API compatibile con OpenAI, ideale per la produzione
  • Ollama — configurazione più semplice, ottimo per lo sviluppo e il deployment su piccola scala
  • llama.cpp — il più leggero, funziona su CPU, ideale per il deployment edge

Parte 13: Rate Limiting e Protezione delle API

Ogni SaaS di produzione ha bisogno di rate limiting per prevenire abusi, controllare i costi e garantire un uso equo. Ecco un’implementazione di livello produzione:

rate_limiter.py — Rate Limiting di Produzione per ClipCraft
"""
Production rate limiting for ClipCraft.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)


# --- Demo ---
print("=== Rate Limiting Demo for ClipCraft ===\
")

# Simulate requests from different users

    ("user_free_1", "free"),
    ("user_pro_1", "pro"),
    ("user_enterprise_1", "enterprise"),

for user_id, tier in users:
    print(f"User: {{user_id}} ({{tier}} tier)")

        print(f"  Request {{i+1}}: {{status}} | {{info}}")

    def handle_webhook(self, event_type, data):
        """Handle Stripe webhook events."""
        handlers = {{
            "checkout.session.completed": self._on_checkout_complete,
            "customer.subscription.updated": self._on_subscription_update,
            "customer.subscription.deleted": self._on_subscription_cancel,
            "invoice.payment_failed": self._on_payment_failed,
            "invoice.paid": self._on_invoice_paid,
        }}

        handler = handlers.get(event_type)
        if handler:
            return handler(data)
        return {{"status": "unhandled", "event": event_type}}

    def _on_checkout_complete(self, data):
        print(f"  Checkout completed! Activate subscription for user.")
        return {{"action": "activate_subscription"}}

        return {{"action": "sync_tier"}}

        return {{"action": "downgrade_to_free"}}

    def _on_payment_failed(self, data):
        print(f"  Payment failed! Send dunning email, grace period 7 days.")
        return {{"action": "send_dunning_email", "grace_days": 7}}

    def _on_invoice_paid(self, data):

        return {{"action": "reset_usage"}}

Parte 15: Scalare verso un Prodotto di Massa

Scalare da un MVP a un prodotto di massa richiede cambiamenti architetturali a ogni livello. Ecco il playbook completo per lo scaling:

Punti Chiave

  • L’asincronia è obbligatoria per il video: La generazione video richiede da 30 secondi a 5 minuti. Devi usare una coda di job con elaborazione in background — l’HTTP sincrono andrà in timeout.
  • Il monitoraggio del progresso costruisce fiducia: Gli utenti devono vedere che sta succedendo qualcosa. Offri sia endpoint di polling sia callback webhook per flessibilità.
  • La logica di retry è fondamentale: I task GPU di lunga durata falliscono più spesso delle chiamate API veloci. I tentativi automatici con backoff esponenziale mantengono affidabile il tuo servizio.
  • Controlla la concorrenza per controllare i costi: Limita il numero di job simultanei. Ogni video costa $0.10–$1.00 in tariffe API — una concorrenza fuori controllo può prosciugare il tuo budget in pochi minuti.
  • Il video costa da 10 a 50 volte in più delle immagini: Prezza i tuoi livelli di conseguenza. Un piano da $10/mese che consente 100 immagini potrebbe consentire solo 10–20 video.
  • FFmpeg è il tuo migliore amico: Usalo per la transcodifica, i cambi di risoluzione, la filigrana e la conversione di formato. Funziona ovunque e gestisce ogni codec.

Prossimo: In GenAI-3, costruirai un SaaS di Generazione Voce e Audio — gestendo text-to-speech, clonazione vocale e pipeline di elaborazione audio.

GenAI-2 البناء: منتج SaaS بالذكاء الاصطناعي

بناء SaaS لتوليد الفيديو

ابنِ ClipCraft — خدمة توليد فيديو جاهزة للإنتاج تعتمد على قوائم انتظار مهام غير متزامنة، وتتبّع للتقدّم، وخلفية (backend) مبنية على FastAPI تنسّق عمل نماذج تحويل النص إلى فيديو.
75 دقيقة متقدم / تطبيقي ستبني منتجًا حقيقيًا وتنشره

ما الذي ستبنيه

في هذا الدرس ستبني ClipCraft — منصة SaaS لتوليد الفيديو. يرسل المستخدمون طلبات نصية، ويقوم خادمك بتوجيه الطلب إلى نموذج تحويل نص إلى فيديو (Runway أو Pika أو Stability AI Video)، ويدير عملية التوليد الطويلة عبر قائمة انتظار مهام غير متزامنة، ويبث تحديثات التقدّم، ويسلّم الفيديو النهائي. ستنفّذ المجموعة الكاملة: خادم API، وخط معالجة الفيديو، وإدارة المهام، وتتبّع التقدّم، والنشر.

توليد الفيديو مختلف جوهريًا عن توليد الصور. فقد يستغرق إنتاج فيديو واحد ما بين 30 ثانية و5 دقائق، ما يعني أنه لا يمكنك استخدام نمط طلب-استجابة بسيط. بدلًا من ذلك، تحتاج إلى بنية غير متزامنة تعتمد على قوائم انتظار المهام، واستقصاء الحالة، وإشعارات الـwebhook.

ClipCraft — نظرة عامة كاملة على المشروع

المكوّن التقنية
خادم APIPython + FastAPI

معالجة الفيديوNumPy (حسابات الإطارات) + FFmpeg (الترميز)

الواجهة الأماميةHTML + vanilla JS

بنية المشروع

أنشئ بنية المجلدات التالية على جهازك. سيُشرح كل ملف في هذا الدرس.

الجزء 1: كيف تعمل واجهات برمجة تطبيقات توليد الفيديو

توسّع نماذج تحويل النص إلى فيديو تقنيات الانتشار (diffusion) من الصور إلى التسلسلات الزمنية. فبدلًا من إزالة الضوضاء عن إطار واحد، تُزيل الضوضاء عن حجم مكاني-زماني — منتجةً إطارات متعددة متماسكة تتدفق بشكل طبيعي. هذا أكثر تكلفة بمراتب من توليد الصور ويستغرق وقتًا أطول بكثير.

مقارنة واجهات برمجة تطبيقات توليد الفيديو (2024–2025)

المزوّد النموذج التكلفة لكل فيديو المدة / الدقة
RunwayGen-3 Alpha$0.25–$1.005–10s / حتى 1280×768
Pika LabsPika 1.0$0.20–$0.803–4s / حتى 1024×1024
Stability AIStable Video Diffusion$0.10–$0.504s / 576×1024
Luma AIDream Machine$0.30–$0.905s / حتى 1360×752

الفرق الجوهري عن توليد الصور

يعيد توليد الصور نتيجةً خلال 2–10 ثوانٍ. أما توليد الفيديو فيستغرق ما بين 30 ثانية و5 دقائق. هذا يعني أنه لا يمكنك إبقاء اتصال HTTP مفتوحًا والانتظار. أنت بحاجة إلى:

  • قائمة انتظار المهام: اقبل الطلب، وأعد معرّف مهمة فورًا، وعالِج في الخلفية
  • تتبّع التقدّم: اسمح للعملاء باستقصاء الحالة أو تلقّي استدعاءات webhook
  • منطق إعادة المحاولة: تفشل المهام الطويلة بشكل أكثر تكرارًا — يجب أن تتعامل مع إعادة المحاولة بسلاسة
  • إدارة الموارد: حدّد عدد المهام المتزامنة للتحكم في التكاليف ومنع الحمل الزائد

النمط المعماري هو: القبول → الإدراج في القائمة → المعالجة → الإشعار. لنبنِ كل جزء.

الجزء 2: خط معالجة الفيديو

قبل دمج واجهات برمجة التطبيقات الخارجية، لنفهم كيف تعمل إطارات الفيديو. الفيديو هو تسلسل من إطارات الصور تُعرض بتتابع سريع. كل إطار هو مصفوفة NumPy من بيانات البكسل. يوضّح الكود أدناه كيفية توليد ومعالجة إطارات الفيديو برمجيًا.

Python 

# processing.py - Video frame generation and processing

import numpy as np
import time

class VideoFrameProcessor:
    """Generate and process video frames using NumPy."""

    @staticmethod
    def generate_gradient_frames(width, height, num_frames, fps=24):
        """Generate a sequence of gradient frames that animate over time."""
        frames = []
        for i in range(num_frames):
            frame = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
            t = i / num_frames  # normalized time 0..1

            for y in range(height):
                for x in range(width):
                    # Red channel: horizontal sweep that shifts over time
                    r = int(255 * ((x / width + t) % 1.0))
                    # Green channel: vertical pulse
                    g = int(255 * ((y / height + t * 0.5) % 1.0))
                    # Blue channel: radial wave from center
                    cx, cy = width / 2, height / 2
                    dist = ((x - cx)**2 + (y - cy)**2) ** 0.5
                    max_dist = (cx**2 + cy**2) ** 0.5
                    b = int(127 + 128 * np.sin(dist / max_dist * 6.28 - t * 6.28))
                    frame[y, x] = [r, g, b]

            frames.append(frame)
        return frames

    @staticmethod
    def apply_fade_transition(frames, fade_length=5):
        """Apply a fade-in at the start and fade-out at the end."""
        result = []
        total = len(frames)
        for i, frame in enumerate(frames):
            factor = 1.0
            if i < fade_length:
                factor = i / fade_length
            elif i >= total - fade_length:
                factor = (total - 1 - i) / fade_length
            faded = (frame.astype(np.float64) * factor).astype(np.uint8)
            result.append(faded)
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def compute_frame_stats(frames):
        """Compute statistics across all frames."""
        brightnesses = []
        for frame in frames:
            avg = frame.mean()
            brightnesses.append(round(float(avg), 2))

        return {
            "num_frames": len(frames),
            "resolution": f"{frames[0].shape[1]}x{frames[0].shape[0]}",
            "avg_brightness": round(np.mean(brightnesses), 2),
            "min_brightness": min(brightnesses),
            "max_brightness": max(brightnesses),
            "total_pixels": frames[0].shape[0] * frames[0].shape[1] * len(frames),
            "memory_mb": round(sum(f.nbytes for f in frames) / (1024*1024), 2)
        }

    @staticmethod
    def add_text_overlay_region(frame, x, y, box_w, box_h, color=(255, 255, 255)):
        """Add a colored rectangle region (simulating text overlay area)."""
        result = frame.copy()
        y_end = min(y + box_h, frame.shape[0])
        x_end = min(x + box_w, frame.shape[1])
        # Semi-transparent overlay
        overlay = result[y:y_end, x:x_end].astype(np.float64)
        overlay = overlay * 0.5 + np.array(color, dtype=np.float64) * 0.5
        result[y:y_end, x:x_end] = overlay.astype(np.uint8)
        return result


# --- Demo: Generate and process video frames ---
proc = VideoFrameProcessor()

print("=== ClipCraft Video Processing Demo ===\
")

# 1. Generate frames (small for demo)
print("1. Generating 12 frames at 32x24 resolution...")
start = time.time()
frames = proc.generate_gradient_frames(32, 24, 12, fps=24)
elapsed = round(time.time() - start, 3)
print(f"   Generated in {elapsed}s")

stats = proc.compute_frame_stats(frames)
for key, val in stats.items():
    print(f"   {key}: {val}")

# 2. Apply fade transition
print("\
2. Applying fade-in/fade-out transition...")
faded = proc.apply_fade_transition(frames, fade_length=3)
faded_stats = proc.compute_frame_stats(faded)
print(f"   Avg brightness before fade: {stats['avg_brightness']}")
print(f"   Avg brightness after fade:  {faded_stats['avg_brightness']}")
print(f"   (Lower because start/end frames are darkened)")

# 3. Add overlay region to a frame
print("\
3. Adding text overlay region to frame 6...")
overlay_frame = proc.add_text_overlay_region(frames[5], 2, 2, 20, 8)
before_mean = round(float(frames[5][2:10, 2:22].mean()), 1)
after_mean = round(float(overlay_frame[2:10, 2:22].mean()), 1)
print(f"   Region avg before: {before_mean}")
print(f"   Region avg after:  {after_mean} (blended with white)")

# 4. Estimate production video sizes
print("\
4. Production video size estimates:")
resolutions = [
    ("720p", 1280, 720, 24, 5),
    ("1080p", 1920, 1080, 24, 5),
    ("1080p", 1920, 1080, 24, 10),
]
for label, w, h, fps, duration in resolutions:
    raw_mb = w * h * 3 * fps * duration / (1024**2)

    print(f"   {label} {duration}s @ {fps}fps: "

# job_queue.py - Async job queue for video generation

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class JobStatus:
    PENDING = "pending"
    PROCESSING = "processing"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

class VideoJob:
    """Represents a single video generation job."""

    def __init__(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        self.id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.style = style
        self.duration_sec = duration_sec
        self.resolution = resolution
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.status = JobStatus.PENDING
        self.progress = 0
        self.created_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.started_at = None
        self.completed_at = None
        self.result_url = None
        self.error = None
        self.retry_count = 0
        self.max_retries = 3

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "prompt": self.prompt[:40],
            "status": self.status,
            "progress": self.progress,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "started_at": self.started_at,
            "completed_at": self.completed_at,
            "result_url": self.result_url,
            "error": self.error
        }


class JobQueue:
    """In-process job queue for video generation tasks."""

    def __init__(self, max_concurrent=3):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.queue = []        # pending job IDs
        self.active = []       # currently processing job IDs
        self.max_concurrent = max_concurrent

    def submit(self, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id):
        """Submit a new video generation job. Returns job ID."""
        job = VideoJob(prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution, user_id)
        self.jobs[job.id] = job
        self.queue.append(job.id)
        return job.id

    def get_status(self, job_id):
        """Get current status of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job.to_dict()

    def process_next(self):
        """Try to start the next pending job. Returns job or None."""
        if len(self.active) >= self.max_concurrent:
            return None
        if not self.queue:
            return None

        job_id = self.queue.pop(0)
        job = self.jobs[job_id]
        job.status = JobStatus.PROCESSING
        job.started_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.active.append(job_id)
        return job

    def update_progress(self, job_id, progress):
        """Update job progress (0-100)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.progress = min(progress, 100)

    def complete_job(self, job_id, result_url):
        """Mark job as completed with result URL."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if job:
            job.status = JobStatus.COMPLETED
            job.progress = 100
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            job.result_url = result_url
            if job_id in self.active:
                self.active.remove(job_id)

    def fail_job(self, job_id, error):
        """Mark job as failed. Re-queue if retries remain."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)

        job.retry_count += 1
        if job.retry_count < job.max_retries:
            job.status = JobStatus.PENDING
            job.progress = 0
            self.queue.append(job_id)
            return f"Retrying ({job.retry_count}/{job.max_retries})"
        else:
            job.status = JobStatus.FAILED
            job.error = error
            job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
            return "Max retries exceeded"

    def cancel_job(self, job_id):
        """Cancel a pending or active job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return False
        job.status = JobStatus.CANCELLED
        job.completed_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
        if job_id in self.queue:
            self.queue.remove(job_id)
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)
        return True

    def get_queue_stats(self):
        """Get overall queue statistics."""
        statuses = {}
        for job in self.jobs.values():
            statuses[job.status] = statuses.get(job.status, 0) + 1
        return {
            "total_jobs": len(self.jobs),
            "queue_length": len(self.queue),
            "active_jobs": len(self.active),
            "max_concurrent": self.max_concurrent,
            "by_status": statuses
        }


# --- Demo: Simulate a video generation workload ---
queue = JobQueue(max_concurrent=2)

print("=== ClipCraft Job Queue Demo ===\
")

# Submit several jobs
prompts = [
    ("A serene lake at sunset with mountains", "cinematic", 5),

# progress.py - Progress tracking with polling and webhooks

import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

class ProgressTracker:
    """Track video generation progress with polling and webhook support."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.jobs = {}
        self.webhook_log = []  # simulated webhook deliveries

    def register_job(self, job_id, webhook_url=None):
        """Register a job for progress tracking."""
        self.jobs[job_id] = {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "progress": 0,
            "stage": "queued",
            "webhook_url": webhook_url,
            "events": [],
            "started": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }

    def update(self, job_id, progress, stage, message=""):
        """Update progress and optionally fire webhook."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return

        job["progress"] = progress
        job["stage"] = stage

        event = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "progress": progress,
            "stage": stage,
            "message": message
        }
        job["events"].append(event)

        # Fire webhook if configured
        if job["webhook_url"]:
            self._fire_webhook(job_id, event)

    def _fire_webhook(self, job_id, event):
        """Simulate sending a webhook notification."""
        payload = {
            "event": "video.progress",
            "job_id": job_id,
            "data": event,
            "delivery_id": str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        }
        self.webhook_log.append(payload)

    def poll(self, job_id):
        """Client polls for current status (the polling endpoint)."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return {"error": "Job not found"}
        return {
            "job_id": job["job_id"],
            "progress": job["progress"],
            "stage": job["stage"],
            "latest_event": job["events"][-1] if job["events"] else None
        }

    def get_full_history(self, job_id):
        """Get the full event history of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            return None
        return job["events"]


# --- Demo: Simulate video generation with progress ---

هذا هو قلب ClipCraft — خادم API الذي يربط بين قائمة انتظار المهام، وتتبّع التقدّم، ومعالجة الفيديو، والفوترة. الفرق الجوهري عن خادم توليد الصور هو النمط غير المتزامن: تعيد نقطة النهاية /api/generate الاستجابة فورًا مع معرّف مهمة، ويستقصي العملاء /api/jobs/{id} لمعرفة التقدّم.

app/main.py
"""ClipCraft API Server - Video Generation SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header, BackgroundTasks
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Optional
import uuid
import asyncio
import time

from .config import settings
from .video_service import VideoService
from .job_queue import JobQueue, JobStatus
from .progress import ProgressTracker
from .billing import BillingSystem

app = FastAPI(title="ClipCraft API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

# Initialize services
video_service = VideoService(
    provider=settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
    api_key=settings.VIDEO_API_KEY
)
job_queue = JobQueue(max_concurrent=settings.MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS)
progress_tracker = ProgressTracker()
billing = BillingSystem()


# --- Request/Response Models ---
class GenerateRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str = Field(..., min_length=3, max_length=500)
    style: str = Field(default="cinematic")
    duration: int = Field(default=5, ge=2, le=15)
    resolution: str = Field(default="1280x720")
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None

class JobResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    message: str
    poll_url: str

class JobStatusResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    progress: int
    stage: str
    result_url: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    estimated_remaining_sec: Optional[int] = None


# --- API key authentication ---
async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    user = billing.get_user_by_key(x_api_key)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key")
    return user


# --- Background video generation task ---
async def process_video_job(job_id: str):
    """Background task that processes a video generation job."""
    job = job_queue.jobs.get(job_id)
    if not job:
        return

    try:
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 5, "initializing",
                                "Loading model and preparing generation")

        # Call the video generation API
        result = await video_service.generate(
            prompt=job.prompt,
            style=job.style,
            duration_sec=job.duration_sec,
            resolution=job.resolution,
            progress_callback=lambda p, s, m:
                progress_tracker.update(job_id, p, s, m)
        )

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 95, "uploading",
                                "Uploading to CDN")

        video_url = result["video_url"]
        job_queue.complete_job(job_id, video_url)

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 100, "completed",
                                "Video ready for download")

        billing.record_generation(
            job.user_id, job.prompt,
            result["cost"], job.resolution
        )

    except Exception as e:
        msg = job_queue.fail_job(job_id, str(e))
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 0, "failed", str(e))


# --- Endpoints ---
@app.post("/api/generate", response_model=JobResponse)
async def generate_video(req: GenerateRequest,
                         background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
                         user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Submit a video generation job. Returns immediately with a job ID."""
    # Check billing limits
    can, reason = billing.can_generate(user["id"])
    if not can:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail=reason)

    # Submit to job queue
    job_id = job_queue.submit(
        prompt=req.prompt,
        style=req.style,
        duration_sec=req.duration,
        resolution=req.resolution,
        user_id=user["id"]
    )

    # Register progress tracking
    progress_tracker.register_job(job_id, webhook_url=req.webhook_url)

    # Start processing in the background
    job = job_queue.process_next()
    if job:
        background_tasks.add_task(process_video_job, job.id)

    return JobResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status="pending",
        message="Video generation job submitted",
        poll_url=f"/api/jobs/{job_id}"
    )


@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}", response_model=JobStatusResponse)
async def get_job_status(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Poll for job status and progress."""
    status = job_queue.get_status(job_id)
    if not status:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")

    poll_data = progress_tracker.poll(job_id)
    estimated = None
    if poll_data and poll_data.get("progress", 0) > 0:
        pct = poll_data["progress"]
        if pct < 100:
            estimated = int((100 - pct) * 1.5)

    return JobStatusResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status=status["status"],
        progress=status.get("progress", 0),
        stage=poll_data.get("stage", "unknown") if poll_data else "unknown",
        result_url=status.get("result_url"),
        error=status.get("error"),
        estimated_remaining_sec=estimated
    )


@app.delete("/api/jobs/{job_id}")
async def cancel_job(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Cancel a pending or active job."""
    success = job_queue.cancel_job(job_id)
    if not success:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")
    return {"message": "Job cancelled", "job_id": job_id}


@app.get("/api/jobs")
async def list_jobs(user=Depends(get_user)):
    """List all jobs for the authenticated user."""
    user_jobs = [
        job.to_dict() for job in job_queue.jobs.values()
        if job.user_id == user["id"]
    ]
    return {"jobs": user_jobs, "total": len(user_jobs)}


@app.get("/api/queue/stats")
async def queue_stats():
    """Get queue statistics (admin endpoint)."""
    return job_queue.get_queue_stats()


@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {
        "status": "ok",
        "provider": settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
        "queue": job_queue.get_queue_stats()
    }

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ClipCraft
"""
Production rate limiting for ClipCraft.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)

الخلاصات الرئيسية

  • عدم التزامن إلزامي للفيديو: يستغرق توليد الفيديو ما بين 30 ثانية و5 دقائق. يجب استخدام قائمة انتظار مهام مع معالجة في الخلفية — وإلا فسينتهي وقت HTTP المتزامن.
  • تتبّع التقدّم يبني الثقة: يحتاج المستخدمون إلى رؤية أن شيئًا ما يحدث. وفّر كلًا من نقاط استقصاء وحالات استدعاء webhook لمزيد من المرونة.
  • منطق إعادة المحاولة أمر بالغ الأهمية: تفشل مهام GPU الطويلة بشكل أكثر تكرارًا من استدعاءات API السريعة. إعادة المحاولة التلقائية مع التراجع الأسي (exponential backoff) تحافظ على موثوقية خدمتك.
  • تحكّم في التزامن للتحكم في التكاليف: حدّد عدد المهام المتزامنة. تكلّف كل عملية فيديو ما بين $0.10–$1.00 من رسوم API — ويمكن أن يستنزف التزامن الجامح ميزانيتك خلال دقائق.
  • الفيديو أغلى من الصور بمقدار 10–50 مرة: سعّر مستوياتك تبعًا لذلك. فخطة بسعر $10/شهر تسمح بـ100 صورة قد لا تسمح إلا بـ10–20 فيديو.
  • FFmpeg هو صديقك الأفضل: استخدمه لإعادة الترميز، وتغيير الدقة، ووضع العلامات المائية، وتحويل الصيغ. يعمل في كل مكان ويتعامل مع كل التنسيقات (codecs).

التالي: في GenAI-3، ستبني SaaS لتوليد الصوت والصوتيات — يتعامل مع تحويل النص إلى كلام، واستنساخ الصوت، وخطوط معالجة الصوت.

"""ClipCraft API Server - Video Generation SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header, BackgroundTasks
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Optional
import uuid
import asyncio
import time

from .config import settings
from .video_service import VideoService
from .job_queue import JobQueue, JobStatus
from .progress import ProgressTracker
from .billing import BillingSystem

app = FastAPI(title="ClipCraft API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

# Initialize services
video_service = VideoService(
    provider=settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
    api_key=settings.VIDEO_API_KEY
)
job_queue = JobQueue(max_concurrent=settings.MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS)
progress_tracker = ProgressTracker()
billing = BillingSystem()


# --- Request/Response Models ---
class GenerateRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str = Field(..., min_length=3, max_length=500)
    style: str = Field(default="cinematic")
    duration: int = Field(default=5, ge=2, le=15)
    resolution: str = Field(default="1280x720")
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None

class JobResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    message: str
    poll_url: str

class JobStatusResponse(BaseModel):
    job_id: str
    status: str
    progress: int
    stage: str
    result_url: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    estimated_remaining_sec: Optional[int] = None


# --- API key authentication ---
async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    user = billing.get_user_by_key(x_api_key)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key")
    return user


# --- Background video generation task ---
async def process_video_job(job_id: str):
    """Background task that processes a video generation job."""
    job = job_queue.jobs.get(job_id)
    if not job:
        return

    try:
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 5, "initializing",
                                "Loading model and preparing generation")

        # Call the video generation API
        result = await video_service.generate(
            prompt=job.prompt,
            style=job.style,
            duration_sec=job.duration_sec,
            resolution=job.resolution,
            progress_callback=lambda p, s, m:
                progress_tracker.update(job_id, p, s, m)
        )

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 95, "uploading",
                                "Uploading to CDN")

        video_url = result["video_url"]
        job_queue.complete_job(job_id, video_url)

        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 100, "completed",
                                "Video ready for download")

        billing.record_generation(
            job.user_id, job.prompt,
            result["cost"], job.resolution
        )

    except Exception as e:
        msg = job_queue.fail_job(job_id, str(e))
        progress_tracker.update(job_id, 0, "failed", str(e))


# --- Endpoints ---
@app.post("/api/generate", response_model=JobResponse)
async def generate_video(req: GenerateRequest,
                         background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
                         user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Submit a video generation job. Returns immediately with a job ID."""
    # Check billing limits
    can, reason = billing.can_generate(user["id"])
    if not can:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail=reason)

    # Submit to job queue
    job_id = job_queue.submit(
        prompt=req.prompt,
        style=req.style,
        duration_sec=req.duration,
        resolution=req.resolution,
        user_id=user["id"]
    )

    # Register progress tracking
    progress_tracker.register_job(job_id, webhook_url=req.webhook_url)

    # Start processing in the background
    job = job_queue.process_next()
    if job:
        background_tasks.add_task(process_video_job, job.id)

    return JobResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status="pending",
        message="Video generation job submitted",
        poll_url=f"/api/jobs/{job_id}"
    )


@app.get("/api/jobs/{job_id}", response_model=JobStatusResponse)
async def get_job_status(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Poll for job status and progress."""
    status = job_queue.get_status(job_id)
    if not status:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")

    poll_data = progress_tracker.poll(job_id)
    estimated = None
    if poll_data and poll_data.get("progress", 0) > 0:
        pct = poll_data["progress"]
        if pct < 100:
            estimated = int((100 - pct) * 1.5)

    return JobStatusResponse(
        job_id=job_id,
        status=status["status"],
        progress=status.get("progress", 0),
        stage=poll_data.get("stage", "unknown") if poll_data else "unknown",
        result_url=status.get("result_url"),
        error=status.get("error"),
        estimated_remaining_sec=estimated
    )


@app.delete("/api/jobs/{job_id}")
async def cancel_job(job_id: str, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Cancel a pending or active job."""
    success = job_queue.cancel_job(job_id)
    if not success:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Job not found")
    return {"message": "Job cancelled", "job_id": job_id}


@app.get("/api/jobs")
async def list_jobs(user=Depends(get_user)):
    """List all jobs for the authenticated user."""
    user_jobs = [
        job.to_dict() for job in job_queue.jobs.values()
        if job.user_id == user["id"]
    ]
    return {"jobs": user_jobs, "total": len(user_jobs)}


@app.get("/api/queue/stats")
async def queue_stats():
    """Get queue statistics (admin endpoint)."""
    return job_queue.get_queue_stats()


@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {
        "status": "ok",
        "provider": settings.VIDEO_PROVIDER,
        "queue": job_queue.get_queue_stats()
    }

"""Video generation service - wraps Runway ML / Replicate APIs."""
import asyncio
import httpx
import os
import json
import time
import uuid
import struct
import zlib
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Callable, Dict


class VideoService:
    """Generates videos via Runway ML or Replicate APIs with demo mode fallback."""

    def __init__(self, provider: str = "runway", api_key: str = "",
                 cache_dir: str = "./cache/videos"):
        self.provider = provider
        self.api_key = api_key
        self.cache_dir = Path(cache_dir)
        self.cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=300.0)
        self.demo_mode = not api_key

    async def generate(self, prompt: str, duration_sec: int = 5,
                       resolution: str = "1280x720", style: str = "cinematic",
                       progress_callback: Optional[Callable] = None) -> Dict:
        """Generate a video from a text prompt.

        Returns dict with video_url, duration, resolution, cost.
        """
        if self.demo_mode:
            return await self._generate_demo(prompt, duration_sec,
                                             resolution, progress_callback)

        if self.provider == "runway":
            return await self._generate_runway(prompt, duration_sec,
                                               resolution, style,
                                               progress_callback)
        elif self.provider == "replicate":
            return await self._generate_replicate(prompt, duration_sec,
                                                  resolution, style,
                                                  progress_callback)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown provider: {self.provider}")

    async def _generate_demo(self, prompt, duration_sec, resolution,
                             progress_callback=None):
        """Create a simple test video file when no API key is set."""
        if progress_callback:
            progress_callback(10, "preparing", "Demo mode: creating test video")

        width, height = map(int, resolution.split("x"))

        # Simulate generation time
        for pct in range(20, 90, 15):
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
            if progress_callback:
                progress_callback(pct, "generating", f"Demo rendering frame {pct}%")

        # Create a minimal valid video placeholder file
        video_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        video_path = self.cache_dir / f"demo_{video_id}.mp4"

        # Write a minimal placeholder file
        video_path.write_bytes(
            b"DEMO_VIDEO_PLACEHOLDER:"
            + prompt.encode()[:200]
            + f":{duration_sec}s:{resolution}".encode()
        )

        if progress_callback:
            progress_callback(95, "finalizing", "Demo video ready")

        return {
            "video_url": f"/cache/videos/{video_path.name}",
            "video_path": str(video_path),
            "duration": duration_sec,
            "resolution": resolution,
            "cost": 0.0,
            "demo": True,
        }

    async def _generate_runway(self, prompt, duration_sec, resolution,
                               style, progress_callback=None):
        """Generate video using Runway ML Gen-3 API."""
        if progress_callback:
            progress_callback(10, "submitting", "Sending to Runway ML API")

        response = await self.client.post(
            "https://api.runwayml.com/v1/generations",
            headers={
                "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}",
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
            },
            json={
                "prompt": prompt,
                "duration": duration_sec,
                "resolution": resolution,
                "style": style,
            }
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        job = response.json()
        job_id = job["id"]

        # Poll for completion
        result = await self._poll_job(
            f"https://api.runwayml.com/v1/generations/{job_id}",
            {"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}"},
            progress_callback
        )
        return result

    async def _generate_replicate(self, prompt, duration_sec, resolution,
                                  style, progress_callback=None):
        """Generate video using Replicate API."""
        if progress_callback:
            progress_callback(10, "submitting", "Sending to Replicate API")

        response = await self.client.post(
            "https://api.replicate.com/v1/predictions",
            headers={
                "Authorization": f"Token {self.api_key}",
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
            },
            json={
                "version": "latest",
                "input": {
                    "prompt": f"{style}: {prompt}",
                    "num_frames": duration_sec * 24,
                    "width": int(resolution.split("x")[0]),
                    "height": int(resolution.split("x")[1]),
                }
            }
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        prediction = response.json()

        result = await self._poll_job(
            prediction["urls"]["get"],
            {"Authorization": f"Token {self.api_key}"},
            progress_callback
        )
        return result

    async def _poll_job(self, url, headers, progress_callback=None,
                        timeout: int = 600):
        """Poll a generation job until completion."""
        start = time.time()
        while time.time() - start < timeout:
            resp = await self.client.get(url, headers=headers)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            status = resp.json()

            if status.get("status") == "succeeded":
                output = status.get("output", {})
                return {
                    "video_url": output.get("url", output.get("video")),
                    "duration": status.get("duration", 5),
                    "resolution": status.get("resolution", "1280x720"),
                    "cost": status.get("cost", 0.05),
                }
            elif status.get("status") == "failed":
                raise RuntimeError(f"Generation failed: {status.get('error')}")

            pct = status.get("progress", 0)
            if progress_callback and pct:
                progress_callback(int(pct * 100), "generating",
                                  "Rendering video frames")

            await asyncio.sleep(5)

        raise TimeoutError("Video generation timed out")

    def get_status(self, job_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Get the status of a generation job (sync wrapper)."""
        return {"job_id": job_id, "status": "unknown",
                "message": "Use async polling for real-time status"}

"""Job queue for managing asynchronous video generation jobs."""
import sqlite3

from typing import Optional, Dict, Any, List
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


class JobStatus(str, Enum):

    PROCESSING = "processing"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"


@dataclass
class Job:

    user_id: str

    duration_sec: int
    resolution: str
    status: JobStatus = JobStatus.PENDING
    result_url: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    created_at: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    completed_at: Optional[float] = None
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None


class JobQueue:
    """Manages video generation jobs with in-memory queue and SQLite persistence."""

    def __init__(self, max_concurrent: int = 3, db_path: str = "jobs.db"):
        self.max_concurrent = max_concurrent
        self.jobs: Dict[str, Job] = {}
        self.queue: List[str] = []
        self.active: List[str] = []
        self.db_path = db_path
        self._init_db()

    def _init_db(self):
        """Create SQLite table for job persistence."""
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS jobs (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                prompt TEXT NOT NULL,
                style TEXT,
                duration_sec INTEGER,
                resolution TEXT,
                status TEXT NOT NULL,
                result_url TEXT,
                error TEXT,
                created_at REAL NOT NULL,
                completed_at REAL,
                webhook_url TEXT
            )
        """)
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

    def submit(self, job_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Job:
        """Submit a new job to the queue. Returns the Job object."""
        job_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        job = Job(
            id=job_id,
            user_id=job_data["user_id"],
            prompt=job_data["prompt"],
            style=job_data.get("style", "cinematic"),
            duration_sec=job_data.get("duration_sec", 5),
            resolution=job_data.get("resolution", "1280x720"),
            webhook_url=job_data.get("webhook_url"),
        )
        self.jobs[job_id] = job
        self.queue.append(job_id)
        self._persist_job(job)
        return job

    def process_next(self) -> Optional[Job]:
        """Move the next queued job to active processing.

        Returns the Job if one was available, None otherwise.
        """
        if len(self.active) >= self.max_concurrent:
            return None
        if not self.queue:
            return None

        job_id = self.queue.pop(0)
        job = self.jobs[job_id]
        job.status = JobStatus.PROCESSING
        self.active.append(job_id)
        self._persist_job(job)
        return job

    def complete_job(self, job_id: str, result_url: str) -> str:
        """Mark a job as completed with its result URL."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            raise ValueError(f"Job {job_id} not found")
        job.status = JobStatus.COMPLETED
        job.result_url = result_url
        job.completed_at = time.time()
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)
        self._persist_job(job)
        return f"Job {job_id} completed"

    def fail_job(self, job_id: str, error: str) -> str:
        """Mark a job as failed with an error message."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            raise ValueError(f"Job {job_id} not found")
        job.status = JobStatus.FAILED
        job.error = error
        job.completed_at = time.time()
        if job_id in self.active:
            self.active.remove(job_id)
        self._persist_job(job)
        return f"Job {job_id} failed: {error}"

    def get_status(self, job_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Get current status of a job."""
        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
        if not job:
            # Try loading from SQLite
            job = self._load_job(job_id)
        if not job:
            return {"error": "Job not found"}
        return {
            "job_id": job.id,
            "status": job.status.value,
            "result_url": job.result_url,
            "error": job.error,
            "created_at": job.created_at,
            "completed_at": job.completed_at,
        }

    def get_stats(self) -> Dict:
        """Return queue statistics."""
        return {
            "queued": len(self.queue),
            "active": len(self.active),
            "max_concurrent": self.max_concurrent,
            "total_jobs": len(self.jobs),
            "completed": sum(1 for j in self.jobs.values()
                             if j.status == JobStatus.COMPLETED),
            "failed": sum(1 for j in self.jobs.values()
                          if j.status == JobStatus.FAILED),
        }

    def _persist_job(self, job: Job):
        """Save job state to SQLite."""
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        conn.execute("""
            INSERT OR REPLACE INTO jobs
            (id, user_id, prompt, style, duration_sec, resolution,
             status, result_url, error, created_at, completed_at, webhook_url)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
        """, (job.id, job.user_id, job.prompt, job.style, job.duration_sec,
              job.resolution, job.status.value, job.result_url, job.error,
              job.created_at, job.completed_at, job.webhook_url))
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

    def _load_job(self, job_id: str) -> Optional[Job]:
        """Load a job from SQLite."""
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE id = ?", (job_id,)).fetchone()
        conn.close()
        if not row:
            return None
        job = Job(
            id=row["id"], user_id=row["user_id"], prompt=row["prompt"],
            style=row["style"], duration_sec=row["duration_sec"],
            resolution=row["resolution"],
            status=JobStatus(row["status"]),
            result_url=row["result_url"], error=row["error"],
            created_at=row["created_at"], completed_at=row["completed_at"],
            webhook_url=row["webhook_url"],
        )
        self.jobs[job_id] = job
        return job

"""Progress tracking for long-running video generation jobs."""
import time
from typing import Optional, Dict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class ProgressState:
    job_id: str
    percent: int = 0
    stage: str = "queued"
    message: str = ""
    started_at: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    updated_at: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None


class ProgressTracker:
    """Tracks progress of video generation jobs for polling and webhooks."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.states: Dict[str, ProgressState] = {}

    def register_job(self, job_id: str, webhook_url: Optional[str] = None):
        """Register a new job for progress tracking."""
        self.states[job_id] = ProgressState(
            job_id=job_id,
            webhook_url=webhook_url
        )

    def update(self, job_id: str, percent: int, stage: str,
               message: str = ""):
        """Update the progress of a job."""
        state = self.states.get(job_id)
        if not state:
            state = ProgressState(job_id=job_id)
            self.states[job_id] = state
        state.percent = min(percent, 100)
        state.stage = stage
        state.message = message
        state.updated_at = time.time()

    def poll(self, job_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Get current progress for a job (used by polling clients)."""
        state = self.states.get(job_id)
        if not state:
            return {"job_id": job_id, "error": "Job not found"}

        elapsed = time.time() - state.started_at
        remaining = None
        if 0 < state.percent < 100:
            rate = state.percent / elapsed
            remaining = int((100 - state.percent) / rate) if rate > 0 else None

        return {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "percent": state.percent,
            "stage": state.stage,
            "message": state.message,
            "elapsed_sec": round(elapsed, 1),
            "estimated_remaining_sec": remaining,
        }

    def get_webhook_url(self, job_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Return the webhook URL for a job, if configured."""
        state = self.states.get(job_id)
        return state.webhook_url if state else None

"""Billing system for ClipCraft video generation SaaS."""
import sqlite3
import uuid
import time
from typing import Optional, Tuple, Dict


class BillingSystem:
    """Manages user accounts, API keys, usage tracking, and video tier limits."""

    TIERS = {
        "free": {
            "monthly_videos": 3,
            "max_resolution": "720p",
            "max_duration_sec": 5,
            "price_per_month": 0.00,
            "watermark": True,
            "max_resolution_px": 720,
        },
        "starter": {
            "monthly_videos": 30,
            "max_resolution": "1080p",
            "max_duration_sec": 10,
            "price_per_month": 19.99,
            "watermark": False,
            "max_resolution_px": 1080,
        },
        "pro": {
            "monthly_videos": 200,
            "max_resolution": "4K",
            "max_duration_sec": 15,
            "price_per_month": 49.99,
            "watermark": False,
            "max_resolution_px": 2160,
        },
        "enterprise": {
            "monthly_videos": -1,  # unlimited
            "max_resolution": "4K",
            "max_duration_sec": 30,
            "price_per_month": 149.99,
            "watermark": False,
            "max_resolution_px": 2160,
        }
    }

    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "billing.db"):
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._init_db()

    def _init_db(self):
        """Create tables if they do not exist."""
        self.conn.executescript("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                api_key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                tier TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',
                created_at REAL NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS generations (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                prompt TEXT,
                cost REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
                resolution TEXT,
                duration_sec INTEGER,
                created_at REAL NOT NULL,
                FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id)
            );
        """)
        self.conn.commit()

    def register_user(self, email: str, tier: str = "free") -> Dict:
        """Register a new user and return their account details."""
        if tier not in self.TIERS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown tier: {tier}")
        user_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        api_key = f"ck_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
        self.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO users (id, email, api_key, tier, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (user_id, email, api_key, tier, time.time())
        )
        self.conn.commit()
        return {"id": user_id, "email": email, "api_key": api_key, "tier": tier}

    def get_user_by_key(self, api_key: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        """Look up a user by API key."""
        row = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM users WHERE api_key = ?", (api_key,)
        ).fetchone()
        return dict(row) if row else None

    def can_generate(self, user_id: str) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Check whether the user can generate another video this month."""
        user = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT tier FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if not user:
            return False, "User not found"
        tier = self.TIERS[user["tier"]]
        if tier["monthly_videos"] == -1:
            return True, "Unlimited"
        month_start = time.time() - 30 * 86400
        count = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM generations WHERE user_id = ? AND created_at > ?",
            (user_id, month_start)
        ).fetchone()[0]
        if count >= tier["monthly_videos"]:
            return False, f"Monthly limit reached ({tier['monthly_videos']} videos)"
        return True, f"{tier['monthly_videos'] - count} videos remaining"

    def record_generation(self, user_id: str, prompt: str,
                          cost: float, resolution: str,
                          duration_sec: int = 5):
        """Record a video generation event."""
        self.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO generations (id, user_id, prompt, cost, resolution, duration_sec, created_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (str(uuid.uuid4()), user_id, prompt, cost, resolution, duration_sec, time.time())
        )
        self.conn.commit()

    def get_user_stats(self, user_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Return usage statistics for the user."""
        user = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if not user:
            return {}
        tier = self.TIERS[user["tier"]]
        month_start = time.time() - 30 * 86400
        row = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) as count, COALESCE(SUM(cost), 0) as total_cost "
            "FROM generations WHERE user_id = ? AND created_at > ?",
            (user_id, month_start)
        ).fetchone()
        return {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "tier": user["tier"],
            "videos_this_month": row["count"],
            "monthly_limit": tier["monthly_videos"],
            "max_resolution": tier["max_resolution"],
            "max_duration_sec": tier["max_duration_sec"],
            "total_cost": round(row["total_cost"], 2),
            "watermark": tier["watermark"],
        }

"""
Production rate limiting for ClipCraft.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {
            "free":       {"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50},
            "starter":    {"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500},
            "pro":        {"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000},
            "enterprise": {"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000},
        }

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\n\n"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\n"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\n\n"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\n"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\n"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\n"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\n"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\n"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\n"
        code += "        if not allowed:\n"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\n"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\n"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\n"
        code += "        return response\n"
        print(code)


# --- Demo ---
print("=== Rate Limiting Demo for ClipCraft ===\n")

limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

# Simulate requests from different users
users = [
    ("user_free_1", "free"),
    ("user_pro_1", "pro"),
    ("user_enterprise_1", "enterprise"),
]

for user_id, tier in users:
    print(f"User: {{user_id}} ({{tier}} tier)")
    for i in range(8):
        allowed, info = limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)
        status = "ALLOWED" if allowed else "BLOCKED"
        print(f"  Request {{i+1}}: {{status}} | {{info}}")
        if not allowed:
            break
    print()

# Show middleware code
mw = RateLimitMiddleware()
mw.get_middleware_code()

"""
Complete Stripe billing for ClipCraft.
Supports: subscription tiers, usage-based billing, webhooks.

Setup:
  pip install stripe
  # Get keys from https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys
  # Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env
"""

class StripeBilling:
    """Full Stripe integration for SaaS billing."""

    def __init__(self, secret_key="sk_test_..."):
        # In production: import stripe; stripe.api_key = secret_key
        self.plans = {
            "free":       {"price": 0,    "name": "Free",       "stripe_price_id": None},
            "starter":    {"price": 19,   "name": "Starter",    "stripe_price_id": "price_starter_monthly"},
            "pro":        {"price": 49,   "name": "Professional","stripe_price_id": "price_pro_monthly"},
            "enterprise": {"price": 199,  "name": "Enterprise", "stripe_price_id": "price_enterprise_monthly"},
        }

    def create_checkout_session(self, user_email, plan_key):
        """Create a Stripe Checkout session for subscription."""
        plan = self.plans[plan_key]
        if plan["price"] == 0:
            return {"status": "free_tier", "message": "No payment needed"}

        # In production:
        # session = stripe.checkout.Session.create(
        #     customer_email=user_email,

        #     cancel_url="https://{product_name.lower()}.com/billing/cancel",
        #     metadata={"user_email": user_email, "plan": plan_key},
        # )
        # return {"checkout_url": session.url, "session_id": session.id}

        print(f"Creating checkout for {{user_email}} -> {{plan['name']}} (\${{plan['price']}}/mo)")
        return {
            "checkout_url": f"https://checkout.stripe.com/pay/cs_test_...",
            "plan": plan["name"],
            "price": f"\${{plan['price']}}/month"
        }

    def create_usage_record(self, subscription_item_id, quantity, action="increment"):
        """Record usage for metered billing (pay-per-use on top of subscription)."""
        # In production:
        # stripe.SubscriptionItem.create_usage_record(
        #     subscription_item_id,
        #     quantity=quantity,
        #     action=action,
        #     timestamp=int(time.time())
        # )
        print(f"Usage recorded: {{quantity}} units on {{subscription_item_id}}")
        return {"status": "recorded", "quantity": quantity}

    def handle_webhook(self, event_type, data):
        """Handle Stripe webhook events."""
        handlers = {
            "checkout.session.completed": self._on_checkout_complete,
            "customer.subscription.updated": self._on_subscription_update,
            "customer.subscription.deleted": self._on_subscription_cancel,
            "invoice.payment_failed": self._on_payment_failed,
            "invoice.paid": self._on_invoice_paid,
        }

        handler = handlers.get(event_type)
        if handler:
            return handler(data)
        return {"status": "unhandled", "event": event_type}

    def _on_checkout_complete(self, data):
        print(f"  Checkout completed! Activate subscription for user.")
        return {"action": "activate_subscription"}

    def _on_subscription_update(self, data):
        print(f"  Subscription updated. Sync plan tier in database.")
        return {"action": "sync_tier"}

    def _on_subscription_cancel(self, data):
        print(f"  Subscription canceled. Downgrade to free tier.")
        return {"action": "downgrade_to_free"}

    def _on_payment_failed(self, data):
        print(f"  Payment failed! Send dunning email, grace period 7 days.")
        return {"action": "send_dunning_email", "grace_days": 7}

    def _on_invoice_paid(self, data):
        print(f"  Invoice paid. Reset monthly usage counters.")
        return {"action": "reset_usage"}

    def get_fastapi_webhook_code(self):
        """Print the FastAPI webhook endpoint code."""
        code = "# FastAPI webhook endpoint:\n\n"
        code += "@app.post('/webhooks/stripe')\n"
        code += "async def stripe_webhook(request: Request):\n"
        code += "    payload = await request.body()\n"
        code += "    sig_header = request.headers.get('stripe-signature')\n"
        code += "    try:\n"
        code += "        event = stripe.Webhook.construct_event(\n"
        code += "            payload, sig_header, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET)\n"
        code += "    except stripe.error.SignatureVerificationError:\n"
        code += "        raise HTTPException(400, 'Invalid signature')\n"
        code += "    billing = StripeBilling()\n"
        code += "    result = billing.handle_webhook(event['type'], event['data']['object'])\n"
        code += "    return {'status': 'ok', 'result': result}\n"
        print(code)

Covers: horizontal scaling, queue-based processing, caching, monitoring.
"""

class ScalingPlaybook:
    """Complete scaling guide from MVP to enterprise."""

    def __init__(self, product="ClipCraft"):
        self.product = product

        print("Focus on:")
